Prerequisite: The FortiDDoS and its service contracts registered with Fortinet (FortiCare) through the FortiCloud support portal, with the warranty and support contract current
What it enables: Firmware downloads from the Fortinet Technical Support site, the geolocation databases (downloaded without a subscription while the system is registered and under warranty), and the IP Reputation and Domain Reputation subscriptions (P3 and P4)
How to put it in place: Register the serial number and contracts on the support portal, then check GUI: Dashboard > Status (License Information); GUI: System > FortiGuard (contracted services and subscriptions)
Source: FortiDDoS-F 8.0.0 Handbook, "Step 5 - Complete product registration, licensing, and upgrades" (registration is required to log in to the support site and download firmware), "FortiGuard" (FortiGuard Subscriptions table), and "Appendix J - Security Hardening" (Registration)

Prerequisite: A path from the Mgmt1 port to the FortiGuard servers: DNS servers that resolve update.fortiguard.net, a default gateway, and firewalls that allow the connection; or a web proxy through the FortiGuard tunnel settings
What it enables: License checks and the IP Reputation, Domain Reputation, and geolocation database updates (P1, P3, P4), and the scheduled FortiGuard updates
How to put it in place: config system dns; set primary <DNS_SERVER>; set secondary <DNS_SERVER_2>; end; check with execute ping update.fortiguard.net and execute traceroute update.fortiguard.net; through a proxy: config system fortiguard; set tunneling-status enable; set tunneling-address <PROXY_ADDRESS>; set tunneling-port <PROXY_PORT>; end
Source: FortiDDoS-F 8.0.0 Handbook, "FortiGuard" (Before you begin: ensure the Mgmt1 port can reach the FortiGuard servers; proxy settings), "Step 4 - Test connectivity", "Status" (Tunnel settings for registration and the reputation subscriptions), and "Appendix P - Checking FortiGuard connectivity"

Prerequisite: A FortiGuard IP Reputation subscription, registered to the FortiDDoS (P1)
What it enables: The IP Reputation address ACL list and its categories (DDoS, Anonymous Proxies, Phishing, Spam, and Tor nodes) that the IP Profile enables; the database is removed from the appliance when the license expires
How to put it in place: Purchase the subscription, register it (P1), and check its expiry date and database version in GUI: System > FortiGuard
Source: FortiDDoS-F 8.0.0 Handbook, "FortiGuard" (FortiGuard Subscriptions table: IP Reputation, available subscription) and "IP Profile" (the FortiGuard IP Reputation service is a licensed subscription; if the license expires, the database is removed); "Status" (no licenses are needed for FortiDDoS operation; IP and Domain Reputation are not required for DDoS mitigation)

Prerequisite: A FortiGuard Domain Reputation subscription, registered to the FortiDDoS (P1)
What it enables: The Domain Reputation FQDN ACL list and its categories (Malicious URLs, Botnet Domains, and Bitcoin Mining Domains) that the DNS Profile enables
How to put it in place: Purchase the subscription, register it (P1), and check its expiry date and database version in GUI: System > FortiGuard
Source: FortiDDoS-F 8.0.0 Handbook, "FortiGuard" (FortiGuard Subscriptions table: Domain Reputation, available subscription) and "DNS Profile" (FortiGuard Domain Reputation subscription)

Prerequisite: FortiDDoS deployed inline (in path) on the protected links, with Tap Mode off
What it enables: Drops, source blocking, and aggressive aging: in Tap Mode FortiDDoS is a passive listener that only simulates its actions, and it does not drop traffic
How to put it in place: Cable the traffic port pairs between the external network and the protected network, and keep Tap Mode disabled: config ddos global deployment; set tap-mode disable; end
Source: FortiDDoS-F 8.0.0 Handbook, "Basic Inline deployment" and "Tap Mode deployments" (in Tap Mode FortiDDoS detects attacks but does not take actions like dropping traffic, blocking sources, or aggressively aging connections)

Prerequisite: A Service Protection Policy (SPP) with the protection subnets of the servers it protects, and the profiles assigned to it
What it enables: Every SPP setting, threshold, ACL, and profile option: an SPP setting applies only to the traffic of the subnets in that SPP, and a profile only to the SPPs it is assigned to
How to put it in place: GUI: Service Protection > Service Protection Policy (create the SPP), then config ddos spp rule; edit <SPP>; config address; edit <SUBNET>; set type ipv4-netmask; set ip-netmask <IP/MASK>; next; end; next; end and config ddos spp rule; edit <SPP>; set ip-profile <IP_PROFILE>; set tcp-profile <TCP_PROFILE>; set dns-profile <DNS_PROFILE>; next; end
Source: FortiDDoS-F 8.0.0 Handbook, "Service Protection Policy Overview", "Protection subnets", "Protection profile settings", and "SPP Profiles Overview"

Prerequisite: Traffic statistics collected while the SPP runs in Detection Mode, and thresholds set from them (System Recommendations)
What it enables: Prevention Mode and adaptive thresholds that drop attacks rather than legitimate traffic
How to put it in place: execute generate-traffic-stats spp <SPP> <PERIOD>; config ddos spp rule; edit <SPP>; set system-recommendation enable; next; end (after the learning period in Detection Mode)
Source: FortiDDoS-F 8.0.0 Handbook, "Step 7 - Deploy the system in Detection Mode", "Step 8 - Generate traffic statistics and set the configured minimum thresholds", "Step 10 - Deploy the system in Prevention Mode", and "Thresholds Overview"

Prerequisite: The address and service objects that an ACL names
What it enables: Global and SPP ACLs that match a source address or a service
How to put it in place: config system address4; edit <ADDRESS>; set type ip-netmask; set ip-netmask <IP/MASK>; next; end; config system service; edit <SERVICE>; set protocol-type <PROTOCOL>; set destination-port-min <PORT>; set destination-port-max <PORT>; next; end
Source: FortiDDoS-F 8.0.0 Handbook, "Address and Service" and "Global Access Control List"

Prerequisite: A model that the documentation names for Automated Distress ACLs (ADACLs): the FDD-3000F, and the FDD-3000G in the 8.0.0 Handbook
What it enables: Automatic Layer 3 and Layer 4 distress ACLs under large floods
How to put it in place: Check the model in GUI: Dashboard > Status (System Information) before planning on ADACLs
Source: FortiDDoS-F 7.0.4 Release Notes, "What's new" (FDD-3000F can automatically create Layer 3 and Layer 4 Distress ACLs); FortiDDoS-F 8.0.0 Handbook, "Auto-Distress ACL" (threshold rates for the FDD-3000F and FDD-3000G)

Prerequisite: A second FortiDDoS of the same hardware model and firmware version, licensed and registered, linked to the first on an HA management port (Mgmt2 by default) directly or through a network (Layer 2 multicast, or Layer 3 with the HA ports allowed), and configured as an active-passive pair
What it enables: Merging and synchronizing traffic statistics between the HA primary and secondary
How to put it in place: config system ha; set mode active-passive; set group-id <GROUP_ID>; set priority <PRIORITY>; set hbdev mgmt2; end on both appliances, with a higher priority number on the secondary
Source: FortiDDoS-F 8.0.0 Handbook, "HA system and network requirements" (two identical appliances, same hardware model and firmware version; Layer 2 multicast and Layer 3 HA communications) and "Deploying an active-passive cluster" (license and register all appliances in the cluster)

Prerequisite: The access profile that an administrator account names, or that the RADIUS or TACACS+ server returns
What it enables: Least privilege for local and remote administrators
How to put it in place: GUI: System > Admin > Access Profile (super_admin_prof only for the administrators who need it)
Source: FortiDDoS-F 8.0.0 Handbook, "Managing administrator users" and "Configuring RADIUS authentication" (any access profile is usable for GUI users; CLI users must have super_admin_prof)

Prerequisite: A RADIUS server (or authentication proxy) for administrator authentication, which for two-factor authentication enforces the second factor and for vendor-specific attributes returns the Fortinet attributes
What it enables: Remote password authentication of administrators, RADIUS two-factor authentication, and access profiles and trusted hosts from RADIUS
How to put it in place: config system authentication radius; set state enable; set primary-server <RADIUS_SERVER>; set primary-secret <SECRET>; set backup-server <RADIUS_SERVER_2>; set backup-secret <SECRET>; set require-msg-auth; end (configure the RADIUS server to require the Message-Authenticator before setting require-msg-auth on FortiDDoS)
Source: FortiDDoS-F 8.0.0 Handbook, "Configuring RADIUS authentication" (FortiDDoS-F supports two-factor authentication for RADIUS; the RADIUS server must enable the Message-Authenticator before FortiDDoS requires it)

Prerequisite: An LDAP server for administrator authentication, with a DN for FortiDDoS access provisioned by the LDAP administrator, reached over LDAPS or STARTTLS
What it enables: Remote password authentication of administrators through LDAP
How to put it in place: config system authentication LDAP; set state enable; set server <LDAP_SERVER>; set port 636; set cnid <CNID>; set dn <BASE_DN>; set secure ldaps; set ca-profile <CA_PROFILE>; end
Source: FortiDDoS-F 8.0.0 Handbook, "Configuring LDAP authentication" (work with the LDAP administrator to determine the DN; LDAPS and STARTTLS)

Prerequisite: A TACACS+ server for administrator authentication
What it enables: Remote password authentication of administrators through TACACS+, and access profiles from TACACS+ custom attributes
How to put it in place: config system authentication tacacs+; set state enable; set primary-server <TACACS_SERVER>; set primary-secret <SECRET>; end
Source: FortiDDoS-F 8.0.0 Handbook, "Configuring TACACS+ authentication"

Prerequisite: A non-default certificate imported on the FortiDDoS to verify the remote server: the CA Profile for LDAPS or STARTTLS, and the remote certificate for Verify Host Certificate on an external connector
What it enables: Encrypted LDAP authentication and verified downloads of external IP lists
How to put it in place: Import the certificate in GUI: System > Certificate > Generate and Import (then select it as the CA Profile of the LDAP server, or as the remote certificate of the external connector)
Source: FortiDDoS-F 8.0.0 Handbook, "Configuring LDAP authentication" (a non-default certificate must be available to use LDAPS or STARTTLS) and "External Connectors" (Verify Host Certificate: choose a pre-configured remote certificate)

Prerequisite: A DoD PKI certificate authority that signs the certificate request generated on the FortiDDoS (or a PKCS12 file it issued), with its root and intermediate certificates installed on the administrators' computers
What it enables: A DoD-issued HTTPS server certificate for the web UI in place of the Factory certificate
How to put it in place: GUI: System > Certificate > Generate and Import (generate the request, have the DoD CA sign it, and import the signed certificate), then select it in GUI: System > Certificate > Web Administration
Source: FortiDDoS-F 8.0.0 Handbook, "Managing local certificates" (Generating a Certificate Signing Request: install the CA's root certificate on all computers that connect; Importing certificates; Using certificates)

Prerequisite: A syslog server or SIEM (for example FortiSIEM) reachable from the management port, listening on UDP or TCP (TCP syslog from 7.0.1), for the event log and the DDoS attack log
What it enables: Off-box storage of the event and DDoS attack logs, and retention beyond the local log disk
How to put it in place: config log setting remote; edit 1; set status enable; set ip-address <SYSLOG_SERVER>; set port 514; set proto tcp; next; end (and the attack log remote server in the feature map)
Source: FortiDDoS-F 8.0.0 Handbook, "Configuring remote log settings" (Event Log and Attack Log remote logging configuration pages), "FortiSIEM to collect DDoS attack and event logs", and "Appendix B - Remote Syslog Reference"; FortiDDoS-F 7.0.1 Release Notes, "What's new" (TCP syslog)

Prerequisite: A FortiAnalyzer with Administrative Domains enabled, on which the FortiDDoS is added or accepted in Device Manager
What it enables: Collection of the DDoS attack log on FortiAnalyzer, in the FortiAnalyzer encrypted (OFTP) format
How to put it in place: On FortiAnalyzer, enable Administrative Domain and add the device; on FortiDDoS: config log setting ddos-attack-log-remote; edit <ATTACK_SYSLOG>; set status enable; set ip-address <FAZ_IP>; set fortianalyzer enable; next; end
Source: FortiDDoS-F 8.0.0 Handbook, "Using FortiAnalyzer to collect DDoS attack logs" (To set up log collection) and "Appendix G - FortiManager / FortiAnalyzer syslog integration"

Prerequisite: An SMTP server that FortiDDoS can connect to as a client (with TLS for SMTPS and basic authentication where the server needs them), and the email addresses of the ISSO and ISSM
What it enables: Alert email for event logs and attacks, and emailed scheduled reports
How to put it in place: GUI: System > Maintenance > Mail Server (SMTP Server, Port, Email From, TLS, and Authentication), and the recipients in the alert email and report settings
Source: FortiDDoS-F 8.0.0 Handbook, "Configuring mail server settings" (FortiDDoS uses the mail server as a client to send event logs and reports; it cannot use RADIUS, LDAP, or TACACS+ to authenticate to an email server)

Prerequisite: An SNMP manager (SNMPv3 with authentication and privacy) that polls FortiDDoS and receives its traps, with its address entered as an SNMP host
What it enables: SNMP traps for thresholds, attacks, and Data Path Resources, and SNMP polling of drop counts
How to put it in place: config system snmp user; edit <SNMP_USER>; set status enable; set query-status enable; set trap-status enable; config host; edit 1; set ip <SNMP_MANAGER>; next; end; next; end and GUI: System > SNMP > Config (SNMPv3: Auth And Privacy)
Source: FortiDDoS-F 8.0.0 Handbook, "Configuring SNMP for remote alarm event trap reporting and MIB queries" and "Configuring SNMP trap receivers for remote DDoS attack reporting"

Prerequisite: NTP servers reachable from the management port, preferably on the protected management network
What it enables: Accurate time stamps for logs and certificate checks; the Handbook makes NTP mandatory
How to put it in place: config system time ntp; set ntpsync enable; set ntpserver <NTP_SERVER>; set syncinterval 60; end
Source: FortiDDoS-F 8.0.0 Handbook, "Configuring system time" and "Appendix J - Security Hardening" (System time: it is mandatory to use an NTP server)

Prerequisite: An SFTP server with an account and folder for FortiDDoS
What it enables: Daily configuration backups stored off the appliance
How to put it in place: config system daily-config-backup; set status enable; set server <BACKUP_SERVER>; set server-type SFTP; set sftp-username <USER>; set sftp-password <PASSWORD>; end
Source: FortiDDoS-F 8.0.0 Handbook, "Setting configuration auto-backup (Daily Config Backup)"

Prerequisite: A cloud DDoS mitigation service provider that accepts cloud signaling, and the network it needs: at least a /24 public subnet with its own ASN and BGP, a firewall that decapsulates GRE to accept the scrubbed traffic, a lowered MTU and MSS, and alternate addresses for the Mgmt1 gateway and the GRE termination
What it enables: Signaling of large attacks to the provider for cloud mitigation when the links approach saturation
How to put it in place: Contract the service, then add the provider's signaling devices in GUI: Global Protection > Cloud Signaling (signaling uses the Mgmt1 port)
Source: FortiDDoS-F 8.0.0 Handbook, "Cloud Signaling" (Requirements); FortiDDoS-F 7.0.4 Release Notes, "What's new" (cloud signaling devices only for third-party service providers)

Prerequisite: A web server that publishes the IP address list file at a URL that FortiDDoS can reach
What it enables: External IP list connectors that feed addresses to ACLs
How to put it in place: config system external-resource; edit <CONNECTOR>; set type address; set status enable; set resource <URI>; set refresh-rate <MINUTES>; next; end
Source: FortiDDoS-F 8.0.0 Handbook, "External Connectors" (URL: full path to the file; a maximum of 20 external connectors)
